trends.title: Semantics becomes core infrastructure
trends.definition: Shared, machine-readable business meaning (semantic layers, knowledge graphs, GraphRAG) becomes a prerequisite for trustworthy AI and agents, with open interchange standards emerging.
trends.rationale: Gartner names semantics one of three forces shaping D&A and predicts universal semantic layers become critical infrastructure by 2030 (EV-0001, EV-0002). Open Semantic Interchange spec released and moved to the Apache Incubator as Apache Ossie (EV-0003, EV-0004). Signals S1, S2, S3.
trends.industry_note: Multi-carrier groups need single definitions of yield, RASK and load factor before agents can answer commercial questions consistently.

trends.title: Platforms converge on open table formats; competition shifts to catalogues and governance
trends.definition: Data and analytics platforms consolidate on open storage formats, chiefly Apache Iceberg, with differentiation moving to catalogues, table maintenance and access control for agents.
trends.rationale: Gartner lists platform convergence as a driving force (EV-0001). Iceberg adoption treated as settled by practitioners (EV-0005), but survey data suggests warehouses remain the primary paradigm for most teams (EV-0006). Mostly tier 4 evidence beyond Gartner.
trends.industry_note: Relevant to commercial data estates through cost and flexibility; no airline-specific evidence yet.

trends.title: Real-time, event-driven data becomes a prerequisite for agents
trends.definition: Batch data delivery gives way to continuous streaming so that agents can act on current state.
trends.rationale: Gartner forecasts data streaming for agentic AI to rise from under 15% in 2025 to over 60% by 2028 (EV-0001). Single primary source so far.
trends.industry_note: Continuous pricing, disruption handling and in-journey offers all depend on current inventory and demand signals.

trends.title: Agents start managing the data estate
trends.definition: AI agents take on data quality, lineage, governance and policy enforcement, including translating policy into machine-verifiable data contracts.
trends.rationale: Gartner trend and prediction on agentic data management and automated data contracts (EV-0001, EV-0002). Forecast-led, little deployment evidence yet.
trends.industry_note: Indirect: frees commercial data teams from stewardship work and improves data readiness for AI.

trends.title: Capability keeps compounding
trends.definition: Frontier model capability continues to improve across reasoning, science, maths and computer use, with the US-China gap narrowing.
trends.rationale: Stanford AI Index 2026 as reported: human-level or better on PhD science and competition maths, OSWorld success from about 12% to about 66%, US-China gap 2.7 points (EV-0007, EV-0008). Confidence held at medium because figures come from secondary reporting.
trends.industry_note: Sets the ceiling for what commercial analytics and agents can do; relevance is general rather than airline-specific.

trends.title: The unit price of intelligence collapses while total AI bills rise
trends.definition: Cost per unit of capability falls by an order of magnitude or more each year, but agentic workloads consume far more compute, so total spend and cost constraints increase.
trends.rationale: Epoch AI and an arXiv study document steep price declines at fixed capability alongside rising frontier running costs (EV-0010, EV-0011). McKinsey finds about 20% of organisations constrained by AI operating costs (EV-0012). Signals S1, S2.
trends.industry_note: Changes the economics of high-volume use cases such as offer personalisation and scenario simulation.

trends.title: Broad adoption, concentrated value
trends.definition: AI use is near-universal and individuals report productivity gains, but enterprise-level financial impact remains rare and flat.
trends.rationale: McKinsey: 80% report personal productivity gains, 37% any EBIT impact (flat), about 6% high performers (EV-0012). Stanford coverage reports 14-26% productivity gains in some functions (EV-0007). Signals S1, S2.
trends.industry_note: The core management question for commercial functions: converting analyst productivity into revenue and margin.

trends.title: Sovereignty, transparency and regulation become strategic variables
trends.definition: Geopolitics, falling model transparency and evolving regulation (notably the EU AI Act) shape model choice, data residency and vendor strategy.
trends.rationale: Gartner ranks sovereign AI first among 2026 D&A trends (EV-0001). Transparency index reportedly fell from 58 to 40 (EV-0009, low-tier secondary). EU AI Act high-risk obligations delayed to December 2027 and August 2028 (EV-0022).
trends.industry_note: European carriers face residency, vendor-concentration and compliance choices for AI used in pricing and customer interactions.

trends.title: The horizon of autonomous work lengthens fast
trends.definition: The length and complexity of tasks agents can complete without human help is growing exponentially.
trends.rationale: METR finds a roughly 7-month doubling over six years (EV-0014), with its 2026 update implying about 3.5-4 months for recent models (EV-0015, secondary). OSWorld gains support the direction (EV-0007). Benchmarks are software-heavy and set at 50% reliability.
trends.industry_note: Indicates how quickly multi-step analytical work (for example building and testing a pricing scenario) becomes delegable.

trends.title: From pilots to scale, with a shake-out
trends.definition: Large enterprises are moving agents into production while many projects are cancelled and agent washing inflates the market.
trends.rationale: McKinsey: 40% of large firms scaling agents, up from 27% (EV-0012). Gartner: over 40% of agentic projects cancelled by end-2027, only about 130 genuine vendors, yet 15% of daily decisions autonomous by 2028 (EV-0013). Signals S1, S2, S5.
trends.industry_note: Argues for selecting agentic use cases by clear value and avoiding vendor claims that are rebadged automation.

trends.title: Open protocols become the plumbing
trends.definition: Agent connectivity standards (Model Context Protocol, Agent2Agent, agent payments) consolidate under neutral open-source governance.
trends.rationale: Agentic AI Foundation launched under the Linux Foundation with MCP, goose and AGENTS.md (EV-0016); A2A joined in August 2026 with over 150 partners (EV-0017); membership reported to exceed 250 (EV-0018). Signal S3.
trends.industry_note: Lowers integration cost for airline systems and makes it easier for third-party agents to transact with airlines.

trends.title: Governing decisions, not just data
trends.definition: As agents act, governance shifts to modelling, auditing and evaluating decisions at runtime.
trends.rationale: Gartner decision governance trend and forecast that modelled decisions will be five times more trusted by 2029 (EV-0001); predicts half of agent failures by 2030 will stem from weak runtime governance and calls for an evaluation stage in analytic workflows (EV-0002). Gartner-only so far.
trends.industry_note: Pricing and offer decisions made or recommended by agents need explicit models, guardrails and audit trails.

trends.title: The customer's agent becomes a sales channel
trends.definition: Travellers and buyers delegate search, comparison and booking to third-party AI agents, making machine-readable offers and agent protocols part of distribution strategy.
trends.rationale: IATA: 49% of passengers have used AI for travel planning, Europe lowest at 35% (EV-0020, secondary); IATA urges airlines to retain control of data and customer relationships as agents reshape discovery (EV-0019); ONE Order positioned as foundation for agentic distribution (EV-0021); AP2 extends A2A to payments (EV-0017). Signals S3, S4.
trends.industry_note: Directly affects distribution control, offer representation and the Offers and Orders roadmap.

items.title: Entry-level analytical work exposed; AI proficiency becomes a hiring criterion
items.description: Evidence that junior, data-gathering analyst roles are contracting and that employers will test AI proficiency. Candidate input to a future workforce or skills trend.

items.title: Physical AI and world models
items.description: Gartner expects agents in physical environments to generate far more data than digital applications by 2029. Possible relevance to airline operations and MRO rather than commercial functions.

items.title: Coding agents shift build-versus-buy decisions
items.description: Organisations report building software with coding agents instead of buying it, which could change how commercial teams source analytical tools.
